_what: SKEPTIC re-run of the stage-skipping (interleaved) QAL power schedule. Written BEFORE any deck in qal/skip4v/ was generated or run. Own directory qal/skip4v, own PYMS_VAE_CACHE=.../vae_cache_skeptic.
_role: Independent re-measurement of the claims in qal/skip4/RESULTS.json. Decks are generated by a byte copy of qal/skip4/skip.py (the netlist generator is the thing under test and is verified by reading the emitted .cir, not trusted). ALL extraction is my own code reading the raw .prn, NOT qal/skip4/extract.py and NOT the .mt0 .measure lines.
what_I_re_run_from_scratch: skip free T=120 dV=1.2 (the headline point)
adj  free T=120 dV=1.2 (the adjacent control at the same beat)
skip free T=300 dV=1.2 and adj free T=300 dV=1.2 (the long-beat divergence: the claim that adjacent HEALS to 77.84% while skip FALLS to 25.18%)
skip free T=200 dV=1.2 and adj free T=200 dV=1.2 (the claimed interior maximum in skip's pull-up at ~T=200)
skip free T=120 dV=1.5 and adj free T=120 dV=1.5 (the dV repeat)

checks_pre_stated.C1_headline: Re-measure worst-gate per-gate settling at EVERY bank at each bank's own boundary, from the raw .prn, with the inherited convention (pull-DOWN pct = 100*(1 - V(o)/rail_k), pull-UP pct = 100*V(o)/rail_k, rail_k = V(rail k) at that same instant, NEVER aggregated). Confirm or correct the reported achieved beat period. The reported answer is NO achieved beat period at 90/75/50% anywhere; a single passing row would falsify that.
checks_pre_stated.C2_overlap_is_real_not_relabelled: The whole proposal. From the raw I(L) and V(rail) waveforms of ONE run, extract as time intervals: [hop h close, hop h current zero] for every hop, and the evaluation window of every bank [its charging hop's close, its own boundary]. Then ask whether hop h's conduction interval overlaps in time with a DIFFERENT bank's evaluation interval, and whether the bank supplying the data during that hop is the bank being drained. A serial relabelling would show the hop interval and the settling interval of the SAME data path strictly one after the other, or a boundary placed after the hop has already ended in both schemes. Also measure the rail LIFE of a hop-charged bank in beats (claim: 2.00 in skip, 1.00 in adjacent) directly from the waveform, from the instant its rail rises to the instant its drain phase closes.
checks_pre_stated.C3_hold_over_the_FULL_window_and_the_END: Measure the held bank's rail over the ENTIRE two-beat window myself (minimum, value at the end, monotonicity), not just the endpoints, and measure whether the bank it FEEDS still settles at the END of that window and not merely at its own boundary. Specifically: evaluate the fed bank's per-gate settling at its own boundary AND at the last instant before the held bank drains.
checks_pre_stated.C4_per_gate_stages_3_and_4: Every one of the 8 gates at stages 3 and 4 (and 5 where it exists) printed individually from the .prn. A chain that settles on average and fails one gate has failed. Report the per-gate spread, not just min/max of the two groups.
checks_pre_stated.C5_adjacent_premise: Does the ADJACENT control actually corrupt the successor's inputs? Measure the successor's pull-DOWN gate drive (the predecessor's HIGH output) across the successor's own evaluation window, and the predecessor's rail over the same window. If the successor's inputs are NOT materially corrupted in the adjacent scheme, the premise of the proposal does not apply and skipping is solving a problem that does not exist -- to be said plainly.
checks_pre_stated.C6_instrument: |I(L)| at each hop's switch-open instant from the raw .prn (gate 1 uA), and the hop current zero located by my own interpolation, compared with the tz the deck was built from. A deck whose switch opens far from a zero is not measuring an LC exchange.

my_expectations_before_running.E1: The headline refutation (no achieved beat period, worst gate in the 20-40% band beyond the ideally seeded heads) will REPRODUCE. Settling that far from 90% is not a marginal call and is unlikely to be an extraction artefact.
my_expectations_before_running.E2: The 2.00-beat rail life and the 'data source is never the draining bank' claim will reproduce, because both are properties of the emitted netlist and the phase PWLs, which I can read.
my_expectations_before_running.E3: MY MAIN SUSPICION, stated in advance: that the claimed 'overlap' is a property of the SCHEDULE only and buys nothing measurable, i.e. that the reported concurrency is real as a statement about which banks are busy when, but that no quantity in the run improves because of it. If so, the honest phrasing is 'the schedule overlaps, the circuit does not benefit' -- and I expect the report's own numbers to already show that. I will check whether the report overstated it.
my_expectations_before_running.E4: SECOND SUSPICION: the A1 stage boundary is min(c_k + T, d_k - EDGE). In the ADJACENT scheme d_k = c_k + T, so adjacent banks are checked 2 ps EARLIER than skip banks at the same T. 2 ps of 120 is small but it is a systematic bias in skip's favour. I will quantify it and say whether any reported comparison depends on it.
my_expectations_before_running.E5: THIRD SUSPICION: skip banks 1 and 2 are BOTH ideally pre-charged and bank 2's rail is ideally held until it drains, where adjacent seeds only bank 1. That is a real asymmetry in skip's favour at depth 1. The report flags it; I will check whether the depth-1 comparison it leans on survives it.

labels: Every number MEASURED (from my own .prn), DERIVED (arithmetic on measured), or ASSUMED.
known_limits_inherited_and_restated: qal/sg13lv_compat.sp zeroes ad/as/pd/ps: junction capacitance is ABSENT. Every capacitance, charge, energy and hop time is a LOWER BOUND and every settling percentage is OPTIMISTIC.
Shallow-stack inverter numbers only. sg13g2_o21ai_1, the ALU's dominant mapped cell, never settles anywhere in the PDK envelope; nothing here generalises to a real library.
The chain propagates a SETTLED alternating pattern, it does not switch a changing input. Inherited from the committed harness.
